topic: 限时写作：原因、办法与双边讨论 · Independent new scenario: a research discussion challenging a common metric
grammarFocus: 因果关系、条件和对比；段落间逻辑与指代。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: The Participation Rate Puzzle
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，非官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数。请先听/读对话，理解大意；然后完成10道题（单选、填空、判断正误/未提及）。听力部分注意说话人之间的自然插话和纠正。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新句练习题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有答案均在原文中有依据。
transcript:
Maya: Thanks for coming, everyone. This is the weekly research meeting for the campus learning project. We need to decide whether to keep using the participation rate as our main measure.

Ben: Right. The participation rate is the percentage of students who attend at least one session each week. Last term it was 72 percent. This term it is 81 percent. The number looks good.

Maya: But does it really show learning? I mean, a student can attend and still not learn much.

Ben: That's true. But it is easy to collect. We just count who comes.

Lena: Sorry to interrupt, but I think we are missing something. Attendance is not the same as engagement. A student might sit in the room and do nothing.

Maya: Exactly. So if we want to measure learning, we need a different metric.

Ben: Wait, I didn't say the participation rate is useless. I said it is easy to collect. Those are different things.

Lena: You're right. Sorry. Let me rephrase. The participation rate is easy to collect, but it may not measure learning.

Maya: Good. So what else can we use? We have the end-of-term test scores.

Ben: Yes, but those come only once a term. They don't show weekly progress.

Lena: What about the short quizzes we give every two weeks? They are quick, and they show what students can do.

Maya: That's a good idea. But if we use quiz scores, we need to make sure the quizzes are fair. Otherwise the metric will be unfair too.

Ben: And if we change the metric, we have to explain it to the teachers. They will ask why.

Lena: We can explain that participation is an input measure, while quiz scores are an outcome measure. Inputs are what we do; outcomes are what students learn.

Maya: I like that distinction. So the participation rate tells us how many students come, but it does not tell us how much they learn.

Ben: OK, but I still think attendance matters. If students don't come, they can't learn.

Lena: True. So maybe we should keep both. Use participation to check access, and use quizzes to check learning.

Maya: That sounds balanced. But we need to be careful. If we report both, people may focus only on the participation rate because it is higher.

Ben: That's a real risk. The participation rate is 81 percent, but the average quiz score is only 64 percent. If we report both, the gap is clear.

Lena: And if we report only participation, the gap is hidden. That's why the metric matters.

Maya: So our recommendation is to report both, but to explain that they measure different things. Participation measures access; quizzes measure learning.

Ben: I agree. But we should also check whether the quizzes are reliable. If the quizzes are too easy, the scores will be high and the metric will mislead us.

Lena: Good point. We can ask two teachers to review the quizzes before we use them.

Maya: OK. So the plan is: keep the participation rate as an access measure, add quiz scores as a learning measure, and review the quizzes for fairness. Any objections?

Ben: None from me.

Lena: None. But can we also look at the dropout rate? If students leave, that is important too.

Maya: Yes, good idea. We can add the dropout rate as a third measure. But let's not make the report too complex.

Ben: Agreed. So three measures: participation, quiz scores, and dropout rate. And we explain what each one means.

Maya: Perfect. I'll write the draft and send it to you both by Friday. Thanks, everyone.

The average score on the end-of-term test.
The number of teachers who review the quizzes.
The percentage of students who leave the course.

grammar.title: 因果关系、条件和对比；段落间逻辑与指代
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 因果：because, so, therefore, that's why 等连接原因和结果；2) 条件：if 引导条件句，主句常用 will/can/may 等；3) 对比：but, while, whereas, however 表示相反或不同；4) 段落间逻辑与指代：用 this/that/these/those 指代前文内容，用 however/therefore 等连接段落。注意：if 从句用一般现在时，主句用 will/can 等；while 表示对比时前后结构常对称。
grammar.example: If we report only participation, the gap is hidden. That's why the metric matters.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The quiz was too easy, ______ the scores were high.
questions.explanation: 前半句是原因，后半句是结果，用 so 连接。
questions.evidence: The quiz was too easy, so the scores were high.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: ______ we use quiz scores, we need to check fairness.
questions.explanation: 表示条件，用 If 引导条件从句。
questions.evidence: If we use quiz scores, we need to check fairness.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: Participation measures access, ______ quizzes measure learning.
questions.explanation: 前后对比两种不同功能，用 while。
questions.evidence: Participation measures access, while quizzes measure learning.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The participation rate is high. ______, the quiz scores are low.
questions.explanation: 前后形成对比，用 However 表示转折。
questions.evidence: The participation rate is high. However, the quiz scores are low.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The quizzes are too easy. ______, the metric may mislead us.
questions.explanation: 前因后果，用 Therefore 表示因此。
questions.evidence: The quizzes are too easy. Therefore, the metric may mislead us.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: We should report both measures ______ people may focus only on one.
questions.explanation: 前后是让步关系，用 although。
questions.evidence: We should report both measures although people may focus only on one.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: ______ the quizzes are reliable, the scores will be useful.
questions.evidence: If the quizzes are reliable, the scores will be useful.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The report includes three measures; ______, it explains what each one means.
questions.explanation: 补充说明，用 moreover 表示此外。
questions.evidence: The report includes three measures; moreover, it explains what each one means.

part1: Do you often take tests or quizzes?
Do you prefer short quizzes or one long exam?
How do you check your own progress?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you measured your progress in learning something. You should say: what you were learning; how you measured your progress; what the result was; and explain why you chose that way to measure.
part3: Why do schools use attendance as a measure?
What are the problems with using only test scores?
How can teachers make quizzes fair?
Should students measure their own learning? Why or why not?

transfer.writing: Some people think schools should measure learning only by test scores. Others think schools should use several measures. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 150 words.
